content.rationale: S4 makes the envelope the one owner of channels, status, and refusal shape; the S4-* clauses fix what that means (stdout for normal lines, one stderr line for a refusal, nothing on stdout when refusing, 0/2 with 1 held back, stop before dispatch), and O1–O5 give the refusal line and the status their exact form. Globals (`--version`, `--help`) are handled before dispatch, so the table never routes them and no route↔help cycle appears. It is the sole writer of both streams (M-output-return): every normal line — a global's or a dispatched handler's returned lines — and the refusal line, rendered here and nowhere else. It calls the refusal, route, help, and version modules and carries the injected context through to dispatch (M-context-injection). The write step is exposed as `emit` so an outcome decided above the dispatch still leaves by the envelope's streams and status.
